faq.title: A few things to know.
faq.q1: Can JobFinder invent things on my resume?
faq.a1: It rewrites; it does not add experience. Every tailored claim is checked back against a record built from the resume you uploaded, and anything that cannot be traced to it is flagged for you before you download. That check reads employers, job titles, dates, credentials and numbers. It is a warning system rather than a guarantee, so read the flags. Skills are the one thing it deliberately leaves alone: using the wording of the job description for something you genuinely do is ordinary tailoring.
faq.q2: Will the file pass an ATS?
faq.a2: The exports are built to be read by a machine: plain text in a single column, standard section names, and no tables, text boxes, images or Word headers and footers. You can also run the ATS X-ray, which reads your finished file back with our own parser and shows you what it found. No tool can promise that a particular employer's screener will pass you — what we can say is that nothing in the file is there to trip one.
faq.a3: There are no accounts, no email and no billing. The app itself sits behind a single access code stored on your device — a door key, not a profile. The free CV scan is outside that door and needs nothing at all.
faq.a4: No. You decide what gets sent, and tailoring happens one role at a time so you can read it first. There is one narrow exception: for a single job board, and only for an application you have already approved, JobFinder can submit it for you. LinkedIn is never submitted automatically.
faq.q5: Can I choose how it looks?
faq.a5: Yes. Pick a layout at any time and the preview, the PDF and the Word file all follow it. Most layouts export the same design to both formats. The two-column ones are rendered in the PDF; their Word file falls back to the closest single-column template, so it carries the same words in a different layout — and the picker says so beside the layout you chose.
faq.q6: Does it really work in Hebrew?
faq.a6: Yes — the interface, the tailoring and both exported files. The PDF is laid out right to left line by line rather than being flipped, and the Word file is tagged so that Word applies Hebrew formatting properly. Resumes that mix Hebrew and English work too.
